storage = rs.Storage.embedded(".rivers/storage/")
repo = rs.CodeRepository(assets=[...], schedules=[...], sensors=[...])
repo.resolve(storage=storage)

daemon = AutomationDaemon(
    repo=repo,
    storage=storage,
    max_ticks_retained=100,
    condition_eval_interval="30s",
)
daemon.start()

# ... later
daemon.stop()

AutomationDaemon is intentionally exposed under rivers._core rather than the top-level package — only the rivers dev / rivers serve CLI commands and tests typically construct it directly.

items.title: Eval Modes
items.text:
Each sensor and schedule can specify an eval_mode that controls how the evaluation function is dispatched:

Mode Description EvalMode.Auto (default) Auto-detects async vs sync. Async functions run automatically on the Python event loop managed from Rust. Sync functions run in-process on a dedicated thread. EvalMode.InProcess Always run in the daemon process. Async functions run on the Python event loop managed from Rust; sync functions run on a dedicated thread. EvalMode.Subprocess Run in a loky subprocess for true parallelism. Requires pip install loky. The subprocess rebuilds the resources from their field values, secrets included.

items.title: Example
items.text:
import rivers as rs

# Auto (default): both sync and async run in-process
@rs.Sensor(job_name="my_job")
def my_sync_sensor(context: rs.SensorEvaluationContext):
    # Runs in-process on a dedicated thread
    return rs.RunRequest()

@rs.Sensor(job_name="my_job")
async def my_async_sensor(context: rs.SensorEvaluationContext):
    # Runs in-process on the event loop
    import httpx
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        resp = await client.get("https://api.example.com/status")
    if resp.json()["updated"]:
        return rs.RunRequest()
    return rs.SkipReason("no updates")

# Force in-process for a sync function (e.g. needs resources)
@rs.Sensor(
    job_name="my_job",
    default_status=rs.SensorStatus.Running,
    eval_mode=rs.EvalMode.InProcess,
)
def my_resource_sensor(context: rs.SensorEvaluationContext):
    return rs.RunRequest()

# Force subprocess for a CPU-heavy async function
@rs.Sensor(
    job_name="my_job",
    default_status=rs.SensorStatus.Running,
    eval_mode=rs.EvalMode.Subprocess,
)
async def heavy_sensor(context: rs.SensorEvaluationContext):
    # Runs in subprocess via asyncio.run()
    return rs.RunRequest()

items.title: Schedules
items.text:
For each schedule with default_status=ScheduleStatus.Running:

  1. Rust parses the cron expression and computes the next tick time
  2. Rust sleeps until the next tick (with periodic shutdown checks)
  3. Python evaluates the schedule function → RunRequest or SkipReason
  4. Rust persists the tick result to storage
  5. Python executes any RunRequests via repo.materialize()
  6. Rust prunes old tick records (keeps last 100)

items.title: Sensors
items.text:
For each sensor with default_status=SensorStatus.Running:

  1. Rust loads the cursor from the last tick in storage
  2. Python evaluates the sensor function with cursor + last tick time
  3. Rust persists the tick result (including updated cursor) to storage
  4. Python executes any RunRequests via repo.materialize()
  5. Rust prunes old tick records (keeps last 100)
  6. Rust sleeps for minimum_interval (default "30s")

items.title: Dispatch strategy
items.text:
At daemon startup, each eval function is classified:

  • inspect.iscoroutinefunction detects async functions
  • Combined with the user's eval_mode setting, this determines the dispatch:
    • Async in-process: the coroutine runs automatically on the Python event loop managed from Rust. Other evaluations run while it waits at await points.
    • Sync in-process: the function runs on a dedicated tokio blocking thread. Up to four sensor and schedule evaluations run at once.
    • Subprocess: the eval function and context data are submitted to a loky process pool. The subprocess reconstructs the context from primitives, rebuilds the resources from their field values (secrets included) and calls the function.

items.title: AutomationDaemon
items.text: Method Description AutomationDaemon(repo, storage, *, max_ticks_retained=100, condition_eval_interval="30s") Create a daemon. max_ticks_retained limits stored tick history per automation. condition_eval_interval is the interval between automation condition evaluations (human-readable duration, e.g. "30s", "1m"). start() Start evaluation loops for all running schedules and sensors. A daemon starts once: another call, from any thread, emits a UserWarning and does nothing, also after stop(). stop() Signal all loops to stop and wait for cleanup. A stopped daemon does not start again: create a new one.

items.title: EvalMode
items.text: Value Description EvalMode.Auto Auto-detect async/sync, both run in-process. EvalMode.InProcess Always run in the daemon process. EvalMode.Subprocess Always run in a loky subprocess.

items.title: DatabricksResource
items.text:
Runs Databricks jobs, and makes assets that run them. Fields are read from DATABRICKS_* environment variables when not given. See the Databricks guide.

from rivers.integrations.databricks import DatabricksResource

databricks = DatabricksResource(host="https://dbc-1a2b3c4d-5e6f.cloud.databricks.com", token="dapi...")

Constructor:

Parameter Type Default Description host str \| None None The workspace URL. token SecretStr \| None None Personal access token. client_id str \| None None OAuth client id of a service principal. client_secret SecretStr \| None None OAuth secret of the service principal. azure_client_id str \| None None Application id of an Azure service principal. azure_client_secret SecretStr \| None None Client secret of the Azure service principal. azure_tenant_id str \| None None Tenant id of the Azure service principal. poll_interval float 10 Seconds between status checks of an active run. poll_timeout float \| None None Seconds to wait for a run to end. None waits until it ends. cancel_on_interrupt bool True Cancel the run when the wait stops before the run ends: after poll_timeout, on an error, or on an interrupt such as Ctrl-C.

The credential fields go to the Databricks SDK's configuration attribute of the same name. A field that is None lets the SDK read its own configuration: environment variables, ~/.databrickscfg, or the Azure and Databricks CLIs. The secret fields are hidden from repr() and from the UI's launch dialog.

items.title: job_asset(job_id, *, name, tasks=None, job_parameters=None, resource_key="databricks", **asset_options)
items.text:
Returns an asset that runs job job_id of the workspace. The asset's function is async, so its step waits for the run without holding a worker of the executor. The job is not read when the asset is made: a wrong job id or task key fails when the asset runs.

repo = rs.CodeRepository(
    assets=[databricks.job_asset(123, name="daily_sales")],
    resources={"databricks": databricks},
)
Parameter Type Default Description job_id int required The job to run. name str required Asset name. tasks list[str] \| dict[str, AssetDef] \| None None Keys of the tasks that get an output, named like the task. Map a task key to an AssetDef to give its output another name or settings; an AssetDef without a name gets the task key. job_parameters dict[str, str] \| (AssetExecutionContext) -> dict[str, str] \| None None Values for the job's parameters, or a function that returns them from the asset's context. resource_key str "databricks" The key of the DatabricksResource in CodeRepository(resources={...}). **asset_options Passed to Asset or, with tasks, to Asset.from_multi(), for example group, partitions_def, or retry. kinds defaults to ["databricks"].

Raises ValueError when tasks is empty, or when two tasks get the same output name.

A run uses the resource registered under resource_key, not the instance that job_asset is called on, so the run's config can override the resource's fields. Without that resource, the code location fails to load with unresolved input and the key, for example unresolved input 'databricks'.

Without tasks, the asset is a SingleAsset. A run calls async_run_job() and records a Materialization with this metadata:

Key Type Description databricks/run_id int The run id. databricks/job_id int The job id. databricks/run_url MetadataValue.url The run page. databricks/duration MetadataValue.duration Seconds from the start of the run to its end. databricks/output/<task key> str One entry for each item of DatabricksRun.outputs.

With tasks, the asset is a MultiAsset with one output per task. A run of all the outputs runs every task of the job; a run of some outputs sends their task keys as only. When the run ends, each selected task that ended with SUCCESS records a materialization with this metadata:

Key Type Description databricks/run_id int The run id of the job. databricks/job_id int The job id. databricks/run_url MetadataValue.url The run page of the task. databricks/duration MetadataValue.duration Seconds from the start of the task to its end. databricks/task_key str The task key. databricks/output str The value the notebook task passed to dbutils.notebook.exit().

The other selected outputs fail with DatabricksRunError. A failed task without an output is logged as a warning. rivers does not retry an asset with tasks.

items.title: run_job(job_id, *, job_parameters=None, only=None, log=None)
items.text:
Runs an existing job, waits until the run ends, and returns a DatabricksRun.

Parameter Type Default Description job_id int required The job to run. job_parameters dict[str, str] \| None None Values for the job's parameters. only list[str] \| None None Keys of the tasks to run. None runs every task. log logging.Logger \| None None Logger for the run's progress, for example context.log.

items.title: submit_run(tasks, *, log=None, **submit_args)
items.text:
Submits a one-time run of tasks, waits until it ends, and returns a DatabricksRun.

Parameter Type Default Description tasks list[jobs.SubmitTask \| dict] required The tasks of the run. A dict has the form of a task in the Jobs API. log logging.Logger \| None None Logger for the run's progress, for example context.log. **submit_args Other arguments for WorkspaceClient.jobs.submit, for example run_name, timeout_seconds, environments. 
run = databricks.submit_run(
    [
        {
            "task_key": "main",
            "spark_python_task": {"python_file": "/Workspace/etl/customers.py"},
            "existing_cluster_id": "0101-123456-abcdefgh",
        }
    ],
    run_name="customers",
)

items.title: async_run_job(job_id, *, job_parameters=None, only=None, log=None)
items.text: run_job for async code. It takes the same arguments, returns and raises the same, and waits without blocking the event loop.

items.title: async_submit_run(tasks, *, log=None, **submit_args)
items.text:
submit_run for async code, in the same way. The asset takes the resource registered under databricks:

@rs.Asset(kinds="databricks")
async def customers(context: rs.AssetExecutionContext, databricks: DatabricksResource) -> rs.Materialization:
    run = await databricks.async_submit_run(tasks, run_name="customers", log=context.log)
    return rs.Materialization(metadata={"databricks/run_id": run.run_id})

repo = rs.CodeRepository(assets=[customers], resources={"databricks": DatabricksResource()})

These methods and the job assets get the state of the run every poll_interval seconds, and log each new state. They raise:

Exception When DatabricksRunError The run ended without SUCCESS. TimeoutError The run did not end within poll_timeout.

When the wait stops before the run ends and cancel_on_interrupt is set, the run is canceled. A failed cancel is logged and does not replace the original error.

items.title: get_client()
items.text: Returns a databricks.sdk.WorkspaceClient for the workspace.

items.title: DatabricksRun
items.text:
A Databricks run that ended with SUCCESS. Returned by run_job, submit_run, and their async versions. A pydantic model.

Attribute Type Description run_id int The run id. job_id int \| None The job id. A one-time run also has one. run_page_url str \| None The run's page in the workspace. duration float \| None Seconds from the start of the run to its end. outputs dict[str, str] The value each successful notebook task passed to dbutils.notebook.exit(), by task key. Databricks returns the first 5 MB of each value.

items.title: DatabricksRunError
items.text: Raised when a Databricks run, or a selected task of a job asset, ends without SUCCESS. The message gives the run's state, the URL of the run page, and the error and stack trace of each task that ended with FAILED, TIMEDOUT, CANCELED, or INTERNAL_ERROR. Use it in a retry policy: rs.RetryPolicy(max_retries=2, retry_on=[DatabricksRunError]).

items.title: DatadogResource
items.text:
A Datadog client, and the hooks and sensor that post events through it. Fields are read from DATADOG_* environment variables when not given. See the Datadog guide for setup and examples.

from rivers.integrations.datadog import DatadogResource

datadog = DatadogResource(api_key="...", constant_tags=["env:prod"])

Constructor:

Parameter Type Default Description api_key SecretStr \| None None API key. The hooks and the sensor need it. app_key SecretStr \| None None Application key, for client.api calls that read data. api_host str "https://api.datadoghq.com" The API endpoint of your Datadog site, e.g. "https://api.datadoghq.eu". statsd_host str \| None None DogStatsD host. None reads DD_AGENT_HOST, else uses "localhost". statsd_port int \| None None DogStatsD port. None reads DD_DOGSTATSD_PORT, else uses 8125. statsd_socket_path str \| None None DogStatsD Unix socket. Used instead of the host and port. constant_tags list[str] [] Tags on every metric and event. In DATADOG_CONSTANT_TAGS, a JSON list.

items.title: get_client()
items.text:
Returns the DatadogClient for the DogStatsD fields. Resources with the same DogStatsD fields share one client per process. Also points datadogpy's process-wide API client at api_key, app_key, and api_host.

client = datadog.get_client()
client.increment("orders.loaded", tags=["source:s3"])

items.title: failure_hook(*, tags=None, text_fn=None, ui_location_url=None, name="datadog_failure_hook")
items.text: Returns a Hook.failure that posts an error event to the Datadog API when an asset step fails. The title is Asset <asset> failed, and the default text quotes the error.

items.title: success_hook(*, tags=None, text_fn=None, ui_location_url=None, name="datadog_success_hook")
items.text:
Returns a Hook.success that posts a success event when an asset step succeeds. The title is Asset <asset> succeeded.

The hook events are tagged asset:<asset> and run_id:<run id>.

Parameter Type Default Description tags list[str] \| None None More tags for the event. text_fn Callable[[HookContext], str] \| None None Builds the event text, in Markdown. ui_location_url str \| None None The code location's UI URL. When set, the event links to {ui_location_url}/runs/{run_id}. name str see signature Hook name.

items.title: run_failure_sensor(*, tags=None, text_fn=None, ui_location_url=None, name="datadog_run_failure_sensor", minimum_interval=None, monitored_jobs=None, default_status=SensorStatus.Stopped)
items.text:
Returns a run-status sensor that posts one error event per failed run. The title is Run <run id> failed, with (job <job>) for a job's run. The event is tagged run_id:<run id>, job:<job> and partition:<partition key> when the run has them, and asset:<asset> for each failed step.

Parameter Type Default Description tags list[str] \| None None More tags for the event. text_fn Callable[[RunStatusSensorContext], str] \| None None Builds the event text, in Markdown. The default lists each failed step with its error, or the launch error. ui_location_url str \| None None The code location's UI URL. When set, the event links to the run. name str "datadog_run_failure_sensor" Sensor name. minimum_interval str \| None None Minimum interval between ticks (default "30s"). monitored_jobs list[str] \| None None Only report runs of these jobs. default_status SensorStatus Stopped Whether the daemon evaluates the sensor.

The hooks and the sensor raise ValueError when api_key is not set. Every event also gets code_location:<name> when RIVERS_CODE_LOCATION_NAME is set, then tags, then constant_tags, and the run id as its aggregation key. Each post has a 10 s timeout and raises requests.HTTPError when Datadog rejects the event: a hook logs the error, and the sensor's tick fails.

items.title: DatadogClient
items.text:
A datadog.DogStatsd client, returned by DatadogResource.get_client().

Member Description gauge, increment, decrement, histogram, distribution, set, timing, timed Send a metric to DogStatsD. event, service_check Send an event or a service check through the Agent. flush, wait_for_pending Send buffered metrics; wait for the background sender. OK, WARNING, CRITICAL, UNKNOWN Service check statuses. api datadogpy's HTTP API client, e.g. api.Event.create(...). Its keys are process-wide; it returns a rejected request as a dict with an errors key.

items.title: dataframely
items.text: rivers.integrations.dataframely validates asset outputs against dataframely schemas. Install with pip install rivers[dataframely]. See the dataframely guide.

items.title: Return hints
items.text:
rivers validates the return value when the return hint holds a dataframely schema. The integration needs no import for this. For a multi-asset output, put the same hints in AssetDef(type_hint=...), and rivers validates the output's value.

Return hint Checked value Validation dy.DataFrame[Schema] polars.DataFrame Schema.validate(frame, cast=...) dy.LazyFrame[Schema] polars.LazyFrame Columns and types when the asset returns; rows when the frame is collected Annotated[frame type, Schema] The frame type As for dy.DataFrame[Schema] or dy.LazyFrame[Schema]

A union such as dy.DataFrame[Schema] | None passes when the value matches one member.

cast is the cast attribute of the schema's nested Config class, and False without one. rivers stores the frame that validate returns: columns outside the schema are dropped, and cast columns keep the schema's types.

Errors:

Case AssetOutputValidationError message The frame fails the schema Asset '<name>' returned a value that does not match '<hint>': <dataframely report> The value is not the hint's frame type Asset '<name>' returned value of type '<type>' but expected '<hint>'

The dataframely report names each failed rule and its number of failed rows. In-process, the exception's __cause__ is dataframely's ValidationError or SchemaError.

Output metadata:

Key Type Description dataframely/schema Json The schema that validated the frame. A dataframely/schema entry that the asset sets replaces it.

The JSON object has these fields:

Field Description name The schema's class name. description The schema's docstring. columns One object per column: name, type (the polars dtype, e.g. "Int64"), nullable, primary_key, unique, description, checks. checks The names of the schema's @dy.rule() rules.

A column check is shown by its rule name, with its bound when it has one, e.g. "min=0" or "regex='^(open|closed)$'".

items.title: validate_output(value, hint)
items.text:
def validate_output(value: Any, hint: Any) -> Any

The function that rivers calls for a dataframely return hint or AssetDef(type_hint=...), and for each dataframely schema in an Annotated hint.

Parameter Description value The asset's return value, or the value of a multi-asset output. hint A dy.DataFrame[Schema] or dy.LazyFrame[Schema] hint, or a dy.Schema subclass.

Returns: an Output with the validated frame and the dataframely/schema metadata, or NotImplemented when hint holds no schema or value is not the hint's frame type.

Raises: dataframely.exc.SchemaError when a column is missing or has the wrong type, and dataframely.exc.ValidationError when a row breaks a rule.

items.title: dbt
items.text: See the dbt guide for examples.

items.title: DbtProject
items.text:
A dbt project. Its manifest defines the assets of assets().

from rivers.integrations.dbt import DbtProject

project = DbtProject(Path(__file__).parent / "analytics")

Constructor:

Parameter Type Default Description project_dir str \| Path required The directory with dbt_project.yml. Made absolute. Raises ValueError without dbt_project.yml. target_path Path Path("target") The directory with manifest.json, relative to project_dir. profiles_dir Path \| None None The directory with profiles.yml, for prepare(), selections, and a DbtResource made from the project. None uses dbt's search. profile str \| None None The profile to use instead of the project's. target str \| None None The target to use instead of the profile's default. asset_def_fn (DbtNode) -> AssetDef DbtNode.output_def Builds the output of each model, seed, and snapshot of the project, also of the ones that a definition does not select. source_asset_fn (DbtNode) -> str \| None None Called with each dbt source that a selected output reads, directly or through ephemeral models. Returns the name of the rivers asset that loads the source, or None for no dep. None adds no dep for sources.

An unknown field raises a pydantic ValidationError, e.g. Dagster's state_path.

items.title: manifest_path
items.text: project_dir / target_path / "manifest.json".

items.title: prepare()
items.text: Runs dbt parse and replaces the manifest in one step, so processes that read it meanwhile see the old file or the new one. Also replaces partial_parse.msgpack. dbt starts from the old one, so it parses only the files that changed. Raises DbtError when dbt cannot parse the project.

items.title: assets()
items.text:
project.assets(
    *,
    select: str = "fqn:*",
    exclude: str = "",
    selector: str = "",
    **kwargs,
) -> Callable[[Callable], MultiAsset]

A decorator that builds a multi-asset with one output per selected model, seed, and snapshot. The project's asset_def_fn builds each output. rivers adds a lineage-only dep on each model, seed, and snapshot that the output refs, by that resource's output name, and on the asset that source_asset_fn names for each source that it reads. The deps that asset_def_fn returns stay. The body must be a generator, or an async generator (see Async); another function raises TypeError. kwargs go to Asset.from_multi.

Parameter Description select dbt's --select. A selection other than the default runs dbt ls once per manifest; the result is cached in the target directory. dbt ls needs the profile, like dbt parse, but does not connect to the warehouse. See Select resources. exclude dbt's --exclude. selector A selector from selectors.yml. Raises ValueError with select or exclude.

Raises FileNotFoundError when the manifest does not exist, and DbtError when dbt ls fails, e.g. without the profile. Raises ValueError when the selection has no model, seed, or snapshot, when an output has no name, or when two resources of the project get the same output name.

When the body runs, each argument that is a DbtResource is bound to the outputs, so its cli(args, context) selects them and yields their materializations. Its commands start from the partial_parse.msgpack in the project's target_path. The body must take the resource as a parameter: a body that makes its own DbtResource instead raises TypeError.

Definition metadata:

Key Description dbt/unique_id The resource's unique id, e.g. model.shop.customers. dbt/relation The relation, e.g. "shop"."main"."customers". dbt/materialized table, view, incremental, seed, snapshot, ... dbt/description The resource's description, if it has one. duckdb/schema, duckdb/table With dbt-duckdb: the table, for DuckDBIOHandler. rivers adds them to the metadata of the output; keys that asset_def_fn sets stay.

The dbt/ keys are the defaults of DbtNode.output_def.

items.title: DbtNode
items.text:
One model, seed, snapshot, or source of the manifest, as asset_def_fn and source_asset_fn get it. A frozen pydantic model.

Field Type Description unique_id str dbt's id, e.g. model.shop.customers. name str The resource name. resource_type str "model", "seed", "snapshot", or "source". props dict The resource's entry in manifest.json, e.g. props["config"], props["meta"], or props["source_name"].

items.title: asset_name
items.text: The default asset name: name, with _v<version> for a versioned model, e.g. orders_v2.

items.title: output_def(**fields)
items.text:
Returns the default output with fields set or replaced. The keyword arguments go to AssetDef. It has no deps: assets() adds them.

Field Default name asset_name group The dbt group. None keeps the definition's group. tags The dbt tags, or None. kinds ["dbt"] code_version props["checksum"]["checksum"] metadata dbt/unique_id, dbt/relation, dbt/materialized, and dbt/description, each when it has a value. 
DbtProject(
    Path(__file__).parent / "analytics",
    asset_def_fn=lambda node: node.output_def(name=f"analytics_{node.asset_name}", pool="warehouse"),
)

items.title: DbtResource
items.text:
A resource that runs dbt commands.

from rivers.integrations.dbt import DbtResource

dbt = DbtResource(project_dir=project)

With a DbtProject as project_dir, each of profiles_dir, profile, and target that you do not give takes the project's value, when it is not None. Fields that still have no value are read from DBT_PROJECT_DIR, DBT_PROFILES_DIR, DBT_PROFILE, DBT_TARGET, and DBT_EXECUTABLE.

Field Type Default Description project_dir Path \| DbtProject required The directory with dbt_project.yml, or a DbtProject. The field holds the directory. profiles_dir Path \| None None The directory with profiles.yml. profile str \| None None Passed as --profile. target str \| None None Passed as --target. executable str \| None None The dbt executable. None runs the dbt-core installed with rivers.

items.title: cli()
items.text:
dbt.cli(
    args: Sequence[str],
    context: AssetExecutionContext | None = None,
    *,
    target_path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> DbtInvocation

A dbt command, not started. With the context of a DbtProject.assets() body:

  • dbt runs the outputs that the run selected: the definition's selection for all of them, or --select with the fqn of each and the definition's --exclude. A --select, --exclude, or --selector in args replaces it.
  • Iteration, sync or async for, yields a Materialization for each output that dbt builds (status success, no-op, or reused).
  • In a build, an output with tests is yielded when its tests finish, and not at all when one of them has status fail or error.

dbt's log goes to context.log, or to the rivers.integrations.dbt.resource logger without a context. target_path keeps dbt's artifacts there; by default they go to a temporary directory that is removed.

Materialization metadata:

Key Type Description dbt/invocation_id Text dbt's id for the command. dbt/execution_time Duration dbt's execution time for the resource. dbt/message Text The adapter's message. dbt/rows_affected Int When the adapter reports it. dbt/tests Json Test name to status (pass, warn, skipped) for the tests on the output.

items.title: DbtInvocation
items.text:
One dbt command, made by DbtResource.cli(). It runs once.

Method Description __iter__() Runs dbt and yields a Materialization per output. After the last one, raises DbtError when dbt failed. wait() Runs dbt to the end. Raises DbtError when dbt failed. __aiter__() async for: runs dbt without blocking the event loop, and yields what __iter__() yields. async_wait() await invocation.async_wait(): runs dbt to the end without blocking the event loop. Raises DbtError when dbt failed.

When the iteration stops before dbt ends, e.g. on Ctrl-C, on a cancelled task, or on a break, dbt gets an interrupt, so that it cancels its queries. It is killed when it still runs 25 seconds later. On Windows, it is ended at once.

items.title: DbtError
items.text: Raised when a dbt command fails. The message names the command and its exit code, then each failed or skipped resource with dbt's message, or dbt's error lines.

items.title: DeltaIOHandler
items.text:
Persists asset outputs as Delta Lake tables.

from rivers.io_handlers.delta import DeltaIOHandler

io = DeltaIOHandler(
    table_uri="/data/delta",
    mode="overwrite",
)

Constructor:

Parameter Type Default Description table_uri str required Base URI for Delta tables. Each asset creates a subdirectory. mode str "overwrite" Write mode: "overwrite", "append", "error", "ignore", "merge", "create_or_replace". schema_mode str \| None None Schema evolution: "overwrite" or "merge". storage_options dict[str, str] \| None None Credentials for remote storage. writer_properties WriterProperties \| None None Parquet writer settings. commit_properties CommitProperties \| None None Delta commit settings. table_config dict[str, str] \| None None Delta table properties. merge_config MergeConfig \| None None Merge configuration (required when mode="merge"). handler_config dict[str, Any] \| None None Useful to pass handler-related custom config (e.g. a pre-initialized SparkSession object, or a DuckDBResource as {"duckdb": ...})

Asset metadata overrides:

These metadata keys override handler defaults per-asset:

Key Type Description delta/mode str Write mode override. delta/schema_mode str Schema mode override. delta/partition_expr str \| JSON dict Partition column mapping. delta/table_configuration JSON str Table properties override. delta/writer_properties JSON str Writer properties override. delta/commit_properties JSON str Commit properties override. delta/merge_predicate str Override merge predicate for this asset. delta/columns JSON list Column selection for reads. delta/version str Table version for time travel reads.

Output metadata:

Key Type Description delta/table_uri str Full table URI. delta/mode str Write mode used. delta/num_rows int Total rows in table after write. delta/size_bytes int Total table size in bytes. delta/write_duration_s float Write duration in seconds. delta/version int Delta table version after write. rivers/schema Schema Arrow schema of the written table.

items.title: Methods for action bodies
items.text: An action receives the asset's resolved handler as ctx.io_handler. These methods expose the same URI and partition resolution the write path uses, so a delete/optimize body targets exactly the rows the materialize path would have written.

items.title: asset_table_uri(asset_name, asset_metadata=None)
items.text:
Returns {table_uri}/{leaf}, honoring a delta/root_name override in asset_metadata. Pass ctx.asset_name and ctx.asset_metadata.

@rs.action(outcome=rs.Outcome.Unchanged)
@classmethod
def optimize(cls, ctx: rs.ActionContext) -> None:
    uri = ctx.io_handler.asset_table_uri(ctx.asset_name, ctx.asset_metadata)
    DeltaTable(uri, storage_options=ctx.io_handler.storage_options).optimize.compact()

items.title: partition_predicate(asset_metadata, partition)
items.text:
Returns a SQL predicate covering the partition(s), honoring delta/partition_expr. Pass ctx.asset_metadata and ctx.partition.

@rs.action(outcome=rs.Outcome.Unmaterialize)
@classmethod
def delete(cls, ctx: rs.ActionContext) -> None:
    uri = ctx.io_handler.asset_table_uri(ctx.asset_name, ctx.asset_metadata)
    predicate = ctx.io_handler.partition_predicate(ctx.asset_metadata, ctx.partition)
    DeltaTable(uri, storage_options=ctx.io_handler.storage_options).delete(predicate)

items.title: partition_filters(asset_metadata, partition)
items.text:
Returns delta-rs partition_filters for the partition(s), honoring delta/partition_expr: a list of (column, op, value) conjunctions, one per partition key. optimize.compact and optimize.z_order take one conjunction per call.

@rs.action(outcome=rs.Outcome.Unchanged)
@classmethod
def compact(cls, ctx: rs.ActionContext) -> None:
    uri = ctx.io_handler.asset_table_uri(ctx.asset_name, ctx.asset_metadata)
    table = DeltaTable(uri, storage_options=ctx.io_handler.storage_options)
    for filters in ctx.io_handler.partition_filters(ctx.asset_metadata, ctx.partition):
        table.optimize.compact(partition_filters=filters)

partition is required: reach these only from a keyed action run. On a non-partitioned asset, delete the whole table instead of building a predicate.

items.title: DeltaAsset
items.text:
Asset base class with the standard Delta maintenance verbs built in. Subclass it, define materialize, and optimize, vacuum, and delete appear as actions, resolved against the asset's DeltaIOHandler (its own io_handler or the repository default). Sets kinds = "delta".

from rivers.io_handlers.delta import DeltaAsset  # also exported as rs.DeltaAsset

class Orders(DeltaAsset):
    io_handler = WAREHOUSE

    @classmethod
    def materialize(cls) -> pl.DataFrame: ...
Verb Declaration Behavior optimize Unchanged + Exclusive + Optional key optimize.compact(), or z_order when z_order_by is configured. With a key, rewrites only that partition's files via partition_filters; without one, the whole table. From the UI or gRPC, the keyless form needs an explicit whole-asset choice. vacuum Unchanged + Exclusive + Keyless Removes files no longer referenced by the table. Table-wide: runs without a partition key on partitioned assets too; a supplied key is rejected. delete Unmaterialize + Exclusive + DownstreamFirst + Optional key Deletes the keyed partition's rows via partition_predicate, or every row without a key — on partitioned assets both forms are valid. From the UI or gRPC, the keyless form needs an explicit whole-asset choice.

A verb requires the asset to resolve a DeltaIOHandler — anything else fails the step with a TypeError naming the requirement. On a table that does not exist yet, optimize and vacuum report ActionResult.unchanged() instead of failing, so a fleet-wide repo.run_action("optimize") skips never-materialized assets; delete still applies its Unmaterialize outcome, so dangling state clears even when the physical table is already gone. A subclass redefining a verb replaces the built-in.

items.title: OptimizeConfig
items.text:
Per-asset overrides via run_action("optimize", config={"assets": {"<asset>": {"config": {...}}}}):

Field Type Default Description target_size int \| None None Desired file size in bytes (None uses the deltalake default). z_order_by list[str] \| None None Z-order by these columns instead of plain compaction.

items.title: VacuumConfig
items.text: Field Type Default Description retention_hours int \| None None Files older than this are removed (None uses the table's retention, 168h by default). enforce_retention_duration bool True Refuse retention windows shorter than the table's configured minimum.
